correctness.rationale: The finite census has a complete justified search domain. Repeated adjacent letters may be deleted without losing a distinct-letter permutation subsequence; canonical first-appearance renaming is unique and has free S5 action. For any t-distinct-letter pattern p, its earliest greedy completion in a length-L universal word leaves a suffix universal for the 5-t complementary symbols; hence the deadline L-m_{5-t} with verified m_1..m_4=1,3,7,12 is necessary. Actual C++17 enum_greedy and enum_subseq source blobs were fetched and Git hashes checked; one maintains greedy progress in 120 target permutations, the other explicit bitsets of all distinct-letter subsequences. Both independently compiled and searched the complete normalized, adjacent-repeat-free trees: zero canonical solutions at 18 and an identical list of precisely 128 at 19. Independent Python checks confirmed all 120 patterns in each 19-word, proper normalization and 16 fixed/56 paired reversal orbits; rank-five lower bound follows from empty 18 and extension argument. A full finite exhaustive proof is warranted because every branch and pruning rule is justified; a mere log or numerical sample would not be.

It is not presented as a general alphabet theorem.
